call_points.text: Management declined to guide FY27 revenue growth or operating margin, citing unpredictable war and forex costs.
July-September guided as a tough quarter financially, with costs high and seasonal volumes lower than April-June.
Standalone EBITDA margin fell 377 bps YoY to 4.6%; PBT margin fell about 320 bps.
War impact on gross margin was larger than the energy-regulation impact, which was about half or less of it.
Two price hikes in April and May partly covered cost inflation but not fully; full effect shows from July-September.
Industry volume grew mid-single digits; Whirlpool gained 30-35 bps market share in refrigerators and washers.
Board to have a full blueprint within 12 months on using the large cash balance, including inorganic options.
Sale of services to Whirlpool Corporation continues until March 2029 on an arm's-length cost-plus basis.
Management said it will not raise prices blindly if competitors hold, citing 2022 market-share losses.
E-waste accrual at a higher rate for about 18 months; an industry-wide resolution would be a big benefit.

guidance.statement: Long-term revenue growth ambition of early double-digit CAGR
Long-run margin in refrigerators, washing machines and AC seen at high single-digit
Large-capacity frost-free refrigerator launch planned for Q2FY27
Full blueprint for use of cash, including capacity, new products, automation and inorganic options, within 12 months
Base ongoing capex about ₹100 Cr plus, subject to new initiatives

industry: Consumer Discretionary > Consumer Durables > Household Appliances

operating_notes.text: Refrigerators are more than 50% of total business and washing machines about 25-30%, with AC still a small proportion.
AC average selling price is roughly 2x that of the other core business.
Industry-wide 20-35% of product components are imported, exposing costs to forex.
Front-load washers grew about 80% in volume with triple-digit basis points market share gain; AC revenue grew over 50%, both from single-digit market share.
Capacity utilisation across all products is about 70-75% annually, so no large capacity capex is needed in the next 6-12 months.
Sale of services to Whirlpool Corporation runs until March 2029 on an arm's-length cost-plus basis.
